findings_qualitative.value: Disk-dominated systems rare (~15%); filaments around radio bubbles in at least six of twelve

evidence.quote: Disk-dominated sources are rare in our sample ($\sim15\%$) with only these two clear examples.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular filaments are gas flows tied to radio bubbles
claims.experiment: Moment and Gaussian kinematic maps of 12 BCGs compared with X-ray/radio
claims.result: Smooth velocity gradients, shallower than free-fall, filaments around bubbles in >=6 of 12
claims.finding: Filaments trace flows in bubble wakes and are decelerated

evidence.quote: Smooth velocity gradients found along the filaments are consistent with gas flowing along streamlines surrounding these bubbles.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas velocities are relaxed in the galaxy potential
claims.experiment: Compare CO dispersion with stellar dispersion
claims.result: CO widths below stellar dispersion in most

evidence.quote: In nearly all cases the molecular gas velocities lie far below stellar velocity dispersions, indicating youth, transience or both.

claims.hypothesis: Circumnuclear gas mass correlates with jet power
claims.result: Tentative correlation not significant after uncertainties

evidence.quote: we do not find a significant correlation between the circumnuclear molecular gas mass and the AGN jet power

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pure outflow lifting of molecular clouds disfavoured in favour of in situ cooling of lifted gas

evidence.quote: Filament-dominated systems are difficult to understand in a pure outflow scenario where molecular clouds are directly lifted from the galaxy centre by the radio bubbles.
This sample is neither complete nor unbiased and we are careful to consider this throughout our analysis.
